headline: Black Hills plans to spend $1.8 billion on new generating capacity to power a proposed Google data center in Cheyenne, Wyoming.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept: company-announced agreements with clear figures, but the data center itself is still only proposed.
importance_line: Other electricity customers in Wyoming are told they will not pay for the supply because Google covers the full cost, the plant is mostly gas-fired, and the data center is still proposed.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by The Economic Times, that Black Hills, a South Dakota-based utility, said on 6 Oct 2026 it signed agreements to power a proposed Google data center in Cheyenne, Wyoming, and plans to spend $1.8 billion from 2027 to 2029 on new generation, including 564 megawatts built for the project. Under the agreement Google covers the full cost of supplying the power so it is not passed to other customers, with deliveries starting in late 2027 and peak demand expected in 2030.
notes: Reuters' own page returned 401, so the url is The Economic Times copy carrying Reuters' bullet points. The Reuters text was read in summary form only.
